mainTopic: Why the Torah needs a special source to disqualify birds used for bestiality or idol worship, and רבי זירא's question about bringing a פלגס
overview: The גמרא pushes back on an earlier proof. It says the words of the פסוק about bird offerings, 'of doves or of young pigeons,' are needed for something else: to disqualify a bird used for bestiality (נרבע) or worshipped as an idol (נעבד). Why would we need a פסוק for that? The school of רבי ישמעאל taught that 'corruption' (השחתה) in the Torah means sexual immorality and idol worship, and that word sits next to 'blemish' (מום) in the פסוק about disqualified offerings. So we might have linked them and said that birds, which a מום does not disqualify, are also not disqualified by נרבע or נעבד. The פסוק teaches that they are disqualified. Then רבי זירא asks a new question: someone vowed a burnt offering from a ram or a lamb and brought a פלגס, a sheep in between the two ages. What is the law? According to רבי יוחנן there is no question. He holds a פלגס is a separate creature (בריה), which is proven from a משנה and from his reading of 'או לאיל'. So the גמרא says the question only applies according to בר פדא, and it explains his view on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse is needed for something else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the earlier proof. It says the פסוק's wording is needed to exclude a bird used for bestiality or worshipped as an idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the verse was needed, it was to exclude a bird that was used for bestiality or that was worshipped.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on a proof it brought earlier. It says the words of the פסוק are not free to teach that point, because they are busy teaching something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A proof from a פסוק only works if the words are 'extra' and free to teach it. Here the גמרא says the words 'of doves or of young pigeons' are needed to disqualify a נרבע or נעבד bird. So they cannot serve as the earlier proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Was needed. Used to show that a פסוק is busy teaching a different point.
To exclude, to leave something out of the rule
An animal or bird that was used for bestiality
An animal or bird that was worshipped as an idol

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new law out of nowhere. It answers an earlier proof by saying the פסוק is already being used to teach about נרבע and נעבד.

phrases.english: When the verse was necessary
phrases.notes: The verse here is the words 'of doves or of young pigeons,' which the earlier proof was based on.

phrases.english: it was to exclude one used for bestiality or one that was worshipped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects a proof from the previous part of the daf by assigning the פסוק a different job.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The earlier proof drawn from the wording of the bird-offering פסוק
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק's words are not extra. They are needed to disqualify נרבע and נעבד birds.

steps.title: Corruption means immorality and idol worship
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins explaining why we would need a פסוק. It cites the 'corruption and blemish' פסוק and the teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל that השחתה means sexual immorality and idol worship, with two proof-verses.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since it is written 'Because their corruption is in them, a blemish is in them,' and the school of רבי ישמעאל taught that wherever 'corruption' is written it means only sexual immorality and idol worship. Sexual immorality, as it says: 'For all flesh had corrupted its way upon the earth.' Idol worship, as it says: 'Lest you act corruptly and make yourselves a carved image.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the reason we might have thought birds are not disqualified by נרבע and נעבד. It first shows that 'corruption' in the Torah means immorality and idol worship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about disqualified offerings puts 'corruption' (משחתם) right next to 'blemish' (מום). The school of רבי ישמעאל proves from two other פסוקים that השחתה means ערוה and עבודה זרה. This links נרבע and נעבד to the laws of a מום, which sets up the mistaken idea in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It could enter your mind to say. This introduces a mistaken first thought (הוה אמינא).
Their corruption. A disqualification mentioned next to מום.
Corruption. Here it means sexual immorality or idol worship.
A matter of forbidden sexual relations
Idol worship

phrases.english: It could enter your mind to say:
since it is written
"Because their corruption is in them, a blemish is in them,"
and the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Anywhere that "corruption" is stated,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא דְּבַר עֶרְוָה וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה;
phrases.english: it means nothing other than sexual immorality and idol worship;
sexual immorality, as it is written:
"For all flesh had corrupted
its way upon the earth";
idol worship, as it is written:
"Lest you act corruptly and make yourselves a carved image";

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining why the פסוק from step 1 is needed by laying out the mistaken first thought.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wherever the Torah says השחתה, it means sexual immorality and idol worship. In the offerings פסוק, השחתה is placed next to מום.

steps.title: Birds have no blemish rule, so the verse is needed
steps.stepSummary: Because השחתה sits next to מום, we might link them: what a מום disqualifies, immorality and idol worship also disqualify, and nothing else. Birds are not disqualified by a מום, so we would wrongly say נרבע and נעבד don't disqualify them. The פסוק teaches that they do.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anything that a blemish disqualifies, immorality and idol worship disqualify. Anything that a blemish does not disqualify, immorality and idol worship do not disqualify. And these birds are not disqualified by a blemish, as the Master said: being unblemished and male is required in animals, but not in birds. So I might say immorality and idol worship also don't disqualify them. The verse teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why the פסוק is needed. Without it, we would have wrongly concluded that birds used for bestiality or idol worship can still be brought as offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since השחתה and מום appear together, one might tie them together: they disqualify the same things. A bird offering does not have to be unblemished or male, so a מום doesn't disqualify it, and by this logic neither would נרבע or נעבד. The words 'of doves or of young pigeons' break that link and disqualify such birds anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: A physical blemish that disqualifies an offering
Being whole and unblemished
Being male
Birds (here, bird offerings)
It teaches us. This shows the mistaken first thought is wrong.

steps.whatToRemember: A bird that was נרבע or נעבד is disqualified as an offering, even though a bird is not disqualified by a מום. We learn this from the words 'of doves or of young pigeons.' Without them, the link between השחתה and מום would have made us think otherwise.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think birds are completely outside the rules of disqualification. The point is that their מום rule is different, and the פסוק makes sure נרבע and נעבד still disqualify them.

phrases.english: Anything that a blemish disqualifies,
phrases.notes: This is still the mistaken first thought, which ties השחתה to מום because they share one פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: דְּבַר עֶרְוָה וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה פּוֹסְלִין בּוֹ,
phrases.english: sexual immorality and idol worship disqualify it,
and anything that a blemish does not disqualify,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין דְּבַר עֶרְוָה וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה פּוֹסְלִין בּוֹ.
phrases.english: sexual immorality and idol worship do not disqualify it.
And these birds,
since a blemish does not disqualify them,
as the Master said:
Being unblemished and male are required in an animal,
but being unblemished and male are not required in birds,
I would say that sexual immorality and idol worship
also should not disqualify them,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the mistaken first thought from step 2 and shows why the פסוק from step 1 is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the פסוק's words are needed to block a mistaken inference
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since השחתה is linked to מום, and birds are not disqualified by a מום, נרבע and נעבד would not disqualify birds.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק 'of doves or of young pigeons' teaches that נרבע and נעבד birds are disqualified.

steps.title: רבי זירא asks about bringing a פלגס
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks a new question. Someone vowed an animal burnt offering from a ram or a lamb and brought a פלגס, an animal between the two ages. What is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא asked: If someone says, 'It is upon me to bring an animal burnt offering of a ram or of a lamb,' and he brought a פלגס, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question from רבי זירא about a vow. Did the person keep his promise if he brought an animal that is neither clearly a lamb nor clearly a ram?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כבש (lamb) is a young sheep up to one year old, and an איל (ram) is an older one. A פלגס falls in the gap between them. The question is whether a פלגס counts at all toward this vow, since it may be in doubt or may be its own separate category.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked, raised a question (an open question that needs an answer)
It is upon me. The wording of a vow to bring an offering.
A burnt offering
A ram, an older male sheep
A lamb, a young male sheep
A sheep in between the ages of a lamb and a ram

steps.whyThisMatters: This starts a new discussion about animals in an in-between stage. It connects to the theme of the daf: is an in-between stage a doubt, or a category of its own?

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira raised a question:
One who says: "It is upon me to bring
an animal burnt offering from the ram
or from the lamb,"
and he brought a palges, what is the law?
phrases.notes: A פלגס is a sheep a bit over a year old, too old to be a lamb and too young to be a ram.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: an animal in an in-between stage.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a פלגס fulfill a vow to bring a burnt offering from a ram or a lamb?

steps.title: According to רבי יוחנן there is no question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי זירא's question does not apply according to רבי יוחנן, because he holds that a פלגס is a separate creature, a בריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי יוחנן, you would not ask this question, because he says a פלגס is a creature of its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows רבי זירא's question. It explains that the question cannot be asked according to רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא asked whether a פלגס works for someone who vowed a ram or a lamb. If the פלגס is its own separate category, a בריה, then it is clearly neither a ram nor a lamb. So according to רבי יוחנן there is nothing to wonder about.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the opinion of...
Don't ask this question; here the question doesn't arise
A creature or category of its own, not part of another category

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not answering 'yes' or 'no' about the vow in a doubtful way. For him the פלגס is certainly its own type, so there is no doubt to ask about at all.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yochanan
do not ask the question,
since he says it is a creature of its own,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the פלגס from רבי זירא's question: it is neither a lamb nor a ram.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָא תִּבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי זירא's question from step 4: it doesn't apply according to רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן, a פלגס is a בריה, a category of its own, so the question does not arise.

steps.title: The source for רבי יוחנן's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: someone who brings a פלגס brings a ram's נסכים, but it doesn't count as his offering. It adds רבי יוחנן's teaching that 'או לאיל' comes to include the פלגס.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the משנה teaches: if he sacrificed it, he brings a ram's libations with it, but it does not count as his offering. And רבי יוחנן said: 'Or for a ram' comes to include the פלגס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that רבי יוחנן holds the פלגס is its own category. It uses a משנה and רבי יוחנן's reading of a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a פלגס does not count for a ram or a lamb, so it is neither one. Still, it needs a ram's נסכים, and רבי יוחנן says this comes from a special extra word in the פסוק, 'או לאיל'. Since a פסוק is needed to include it, it must be its own type and not a doubtful ram.

keyTerms.meaning: The flour, oil and wine brought together with a ram offering
It does not count toward the offering he owes
To include something that would otherwise be left out

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows why there is no doubt for רבי יוחנן. The תורה itself treats the פלגס as a separate case that needs its own inclusion.

phrases.english: as we learned in a Mishnah: If he sacrificed it,
phrases.notes: 'It' means a פלגס, brought by someone who owed a lamb or a ram.

phrases.english: he brings with it the libations of a ram,
but it does not count for him as his offering.
And Rabbi Yochanan said:
"Or for a ram" comes to include the palges.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 5's claim that רבי יוחנן holds a פלגס is a בריה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that a פלגס is its own category
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in פרה about bringing a פלגס, and רבי יוחנן's reading of 'או לאיל'

steps.title: The question is only according to בר פדא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to explain that רבי זירא's question only applies according to בר פדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: When you ask the question, it is according to בר פדא.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is preparing to explain how the question works according to בר פדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since there is no question according to רבי יוחנן, the question must follow a different opinion. The גמרא now points to בר פדא. It will next explain his view and why it creates a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: When you do ask the question, here is where it applies

phrases.english: When you ask the question,
it is according to Bar Padda,

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי תִּבְּעֵי לָךְ אַלִּיבָּא דְּבַר פְּדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 5: the question doesn't apply for רבי יוחנן, so it is placed according to בר פדא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי זירא's question applies according to בר פדא.
